title: Forward reasoning with have
summary: Introduce an intermediate fact with have and close the goal with exact.
code: theorem modus_ponens_chain {P Q R : Prop} (hp : P) (hpq : P -> Q) (hqr : Q -> R) : R := by
triggers: build an intermediate lemma inside a proof with have
chain implications forward before closing with exact
prompts: Given P, P -> Q, and Q -> R, derive R using an explicit intermediate fact for Q.
Use forward reasoning with have and exact rather than backward apply.
invariant: have introduces a proven local hypothesis into the context for subsequent steps.
mantra: Name the stepping-stone fact with have, then finish with exact.
pitfalls: Applying hqr directly to hp fails because hp has type P, not Q.
Omitting exact on the final term leaves an unused expression instead of closing the goal.

anchors.name: Forward have step
anchors.trick: Bind hq : Q := hpq hp, then pass hq to hqr.

mutations.explanation: hqr expects Q, but hp has type P.
